t: Section 801(f) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2399), as most recently amended by section 1214 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92; 129 Stat. 1045), is further amended by striking “December 31, 2016” and inserting “December 31, 2018”.

fable.w: This section only extends an existing authority's expiration date by changing one date to another. The tempting reading is that the underlying authority being extended might involve outside parties, but nothing in this text provides for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: is further amended by striking “December 31, 2016” and inserting “December 31, 2018”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that extends a deadline date in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely an internal legislative adjustment of a date.

opus.w: This section only moves a sunset date in an earlier defense law from 2016 to 2018. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. It might be tempting to label it based on what the amended law covers, but the text of this section involves no outside parties at all.

It doesn't mention consulting, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or any party outside the federal government.
